subject: Collapsing markers into groups with zero recombination

messages.author: cd14fa6322656cd5
messages.subject: Collapsing markers into groups with zero recombination
parts:
Dear Karl,



I've collected genotypes from ~125 recombinant doubled haploids at
~5000 polymorphic markers. Also, on average ~10% of the genotypes are
missing per individual. I'm aware that I won't have nearly enough
recombination to resolve most of the markers, but I'd still like to
build a genetic map from these data...having all these markers mapped
will help me assign sequence scaffolds to linkage groups, and I'm
planning to add a lot more recombinants in the the future.



I understand the problems of having lots of markers with no
recombination between them for genetic map construction. Therefore,
I'm planning to collapse these markers into groups of markers with no
recombination and make the map with these groups. I've been playing
around with pipelines for collapsing these markers into groups and
building a consensus genotype for each group. I've done it with some
crude Perl scripts, but I'm wondering if there's a more sophisticated
way to do it directly in rqtl.



I'm curious to hear what you think about this plan, and if you can
recommend an rqtl pipeline for grouping the markers with no
recombination and building the consensus genotype for each group. I'm
aware of and have tried findDupMarkers, but its utility is limited by
the abundance of missing genotypes. I'm thinking about some
combination of formLinkageGroups(max.rf=0) and fill.geno(). However,
I'm concerned about the transitive property of formLinkageGroups and
am not sure if fill.geno() will work. Any advice would be greatly
appreciated!



Best,

Mike

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Collapsing markers into groups with zero recombination
parts:
You can't use fill.geno() until you have a map. It uses genotypes at surrounding markers in order to impute missing data, but until you have a map, you can't know which markers are "surrounding".

R/qtl doesn't really have anything to offer except findDupMarkers. I would first try to form linkage groups and then study whether there are some markers that you can omit from consideration until later. But if two markers are matching at all individuals that they are not missing, but they are missing genotypes at different sets of markers, you can't really trust that they'll map to exactly the same location, and so I wouldn't want to just omit one of them from the map construction effort.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Collapsing markers into groups with zero recombination
parts:
I would use findDupMarkers with exact.only=FALSE and adjacent.only=FALSE.

data(hyper)
dupmark <- findDupMarkers(hyper, exact.only=FALSE, adjacent.only=FALSE)
hypersub <- drop.markers(hyper, unlist(dupmark))

karl
